children: Strong institutional demand pushes subscriptions to 5.7 times as investors assess India’s largest exchange against global peers

India’s National Stock Exchange (NSE) has attracted bids worth more than10 billion USD for its 2.3 billion USD initial public offering (IPO), with investors subscribing 5.7 times the shares on offer by 21 September, despite the exchange carrying a higher earnings multiple than major US listed peers.

The NSE received bids for 505.81 million shares against 88.64 million shares offered, according to news reports. The IPO is the largest public share sale in India so far in 2026 and the country’s second largest IPO after Hyundai Motor India’s 3.3 billion USD issue in 2024.

The exchange had also raised Rs 6,750 crore from anchor investors before the public issue. The anchor book included institutions such as the Monetary Authority of Singapore, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Life Insurance Corporation of India.

The IPO has been in preparation since 2016 and offers investors exposure to India’s expanding participation in capital markets. India’s Economic Survey has said the share of equity and mutual funds in annual household financial savings increased to 15.2 per cent in the financial year ended March 2025, from 2 per cent in the financial year ended March 2012.

At the upper end of its IPO price band, NSE is valued at a price to earnings multiple of 42.9 times based on its financial year 2026 earnings per share, according to Yes Securities data cited by news reports. This compares with less than 24 times for US stock exchange companies. Nasdaq trades at 23.6 times earnings, while Intercontinental Exchange trades at 21.9 times, according to London Stock Exchange Group data. NSE’s market position remains a key factor behind investor interest.

The exchange commands about 93 per cent of India’s cash market and nearly 100 per cent of equity futures trading, while accounting for about 75 per cent of equity options trading, according to its IPO filing. The exchange’s FY2026 revenue fell 3.1 per cent, while net profit declined 15.5 per cent as derivatives activity weakened following regulatory changes affecting options trading.
